title: UMAP
description: Nonlinear dimensionality reduction based on Riemannian geometry and algebraic topology.
name: UMAP
summary: UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a general-purpose non-linear dimensionality reduction algorithm. It models high-dimensional manifolds and projects them to lower dimensions while preserving both local and global structure.
use_when: Visualizing complex, non-linear high-dimensional embeddings in 2D or 3D spaces.
avoid_when: Preserving strict linear coordinate scales is necessary, or quick linear projections are preferred.
pros: Preserves both local clustering and global distance structures better than t-SNE.
Computationally efficient, scaling well to millions of high-dimensional samples.
Can embed new unseen data points into the established manifold space.
cons: Relatively complex mathematical foundation, making tuning parameters non-trivial.
Can create artificial cluster structures if hyperparameters are set incorrectly.
Stochastic nature yields slightly different representations across runs without seeding.

key_hyperparams.name: n_neighbors
key_hyperparams.note: Controls the balance between local and global structure. Larger values preserve global structure.

quick_start:
import umap
import numpy as np

X = np.random.rand(100, 20)
reducer = umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1)
embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X)
